result.rationale: In group.js, removeMember calls self.findMembers() with the unchanged offset; findMembers clamps offset as Math.min(this.get('user_count'), ...) against the stale pre-fetch user_count, so after deleting the last member of the final page the request uses an out-of-range offset and the server (groups_controller#members applies limit/offset without clamping) returns an empty member list, leaving the UI on an empty last page. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff.

judged_text: removeMember refetches with the unchanged offset, and findMembers clamps offset against the pre-fetch user_count, so removing the only member on the last page leaves the UI parked on an out-of-range offset. An admin who deletes the last member shown on the final page gets an empty member list (e.g. '2/2' with zero rows) after confirming, and must click 'previous' to see the remaining members.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, after a successful DELETE it calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset` (models/group.js). `findMembers()` computes `offset` using `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), this.get("offset"))`, but `user_count` is still the *pre-delete* value until the refetch completes. If the admin removes the only/last member on the last page (e.g. `offset=50, limit=50, user_count=51`), the refetch still requests `offset=50`; the server (`GroupsController#members`) uses the given offset directly and can return an empty `members` array with `meta.total` reduced, leaving the UI at `currentPage`/`totalPages` showing the last page (e.g. 2/2) but with zero rows until the user clicks “previous”.
